data.name: Boniface
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'bonus' (good) and 'facere' (to make). The name Boniface means 'good maker' or 'one who makes good'. It was the name given to Saint Boniface, an English monk who traveled to Germany in the 7th century and converted many to Christianity.

in_hebrew.name: בוניפאציוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם בוניפאציוס מקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'הוא שעושה טוב' או 'מביא טוב'. השם נגזר מהמילים הלטיניות 'בונוס' שפירושו טוב ו'פאצ'ר' שפירושו עושה. השם בוניפאציוס היה נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים בימי הביניים והיה קשור לקדוש בוניפאציוס, מיסיונר נוצרי מהמאה ה-8 לספירה.

in_greek.name: Βονιφάτιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βονιφάτιος προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Bonifacius και σημαίνει 'Αυτός που κάνει καλό' ή 'Καλοποιός'. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό ανάμεσα στους Χριστιανούς κατά τον Μεσαίωνα και συνδέθηκε με τον Άγιο Βονιφάτιο, έναν Χριστιανικό ιεραπόστολο του 8ου αιώνα μ.Χ.

in_latin.name: Bonifacius
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Bonifacius is derived from the Latin words 'bonus' meaning good and 'facere' meaning to do. It signifies one who does good or a good-doer. This name was popular among Christians during the Middle Ages and is associated with Saint Boniface, a Christian missionary of the 8th century AD.

in_english.name: Boniface
in_english.meaning: He who does good, brings good
in_english.long_meaning: The name Boniface originates from the Latin name Bonifacius, which means 'he who does good' or 'bringer of good'. It is derived from the Latin words 'bonus' meaning good and 'facere' meaning to do. The name Boniface has been used in Christian tradition since the Middle Ages and is associated with Saint Boniface, a missionary who converted the Germanic tribes to Christianity in the 8th century. The name symbolizes kindness, generosity, and spiritual guidance.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Boniface is remembered as the Apostle of Germany, having significantly contributed to spreading Christianity throughout the Germanic lands. He is credited with converting ethelings (nobles) and their peoples, establishing monasteries, and performing miracles. Through his efforts, he played a crucial role in laying the foundation for the Christianization of what is now modern-day Germany.
data.spiritual_significance: Boniface's life and work embodied the spirit of bringing good—that is, God's love—to people. Through his dedication to spreading the faith, he not only opened the hearts of the Germanic people to Christianity but also provided them with a foundation for spiritual growth. His legacy continues to inspire those who strive to follow in his footsteps and make the world a better place.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Boniface was a Frankish monk and bishop in the 8th century. The name Boniface carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Boniface was born around 672 in Devonshire, England, and was educated in France. He became a monk and eventually a bishop. He is best known for his missionary work in Germany, where he converted many people to Christianity. He was martyred in 754.

trends: Boniface is a common name in Germany and other European countries
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Boniface remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Mary Boniface in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Boniface, which means "Good, generous". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Boniface: Meaning 'good or noble in God.' A monk and bishop who converted the Germans to Christianity, symbolizing dedication and devotion to the divine will.
